page: Amazon Web Services c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core, accompanied by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Memory capacity measures 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, contains no bundled local storage, and includes zero hardware acceleration GPUs.

Benchmark results show strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2817.37, placing it in the top 25 percent. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and AVX-512 BF16, which facilitate high throughput on small-model machine learning inference tasks; prompt processing on a 135M parameter model reaches 3048.53 tokens per second, while text generation reaches 355.9 tokens per second (top 10 percent). General multi-core tests, such as Geekbench multi-core (12184.0) and PassMark CPU (36580.31), settle in the middle 50 percent alongside memory bandwidth benchmarks that register 62.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.81 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes.

Because the server has a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes for persistent data, workloads with heavy local storage demands or large in-memory working sets require consideration of external I/O boundaries. The c7a.4xlarge demonstrates balanced hardware cost efficiency for CPU-bound computations, software compilation (22229.0 on Clang compiling), cryptographic processing via AES and VAES hardware instructions, static web serving (20.88 GB/sec throughput), and small-model CPU inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs, 1 thread per core) and 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, it maintains a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation. The platform lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, relying on 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for interconnectivity. Benchmarks highlight upper-quartile stress-ng single-core performance (2817.37) and top-decile text generation throughput for small 135M language models (355.9 tokens/sec) due to AVX-512 and BF16 vector extensions. Standard multi-core, memory bandwidth, and data compression benchmarks place solidly in the middle tier. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive local storage or deep memory pools, including software compilation pipelines, web serving, microservices, and quantized CPU inference.
